skills.name: Measure mass and convert between units of mass

note.text:
Mass is measured with a beam balance, a lever arm balance or an electronic (top-pan) balance.
Before weighing, check the balance reads zero (adjust or press 'tare').
Units: 1 t = 1000 kg, 1 kg = 1000 g, 1 g = 1000 mg.
Mass of a liquid by difference: weigh the empty container, then container + liquid, and subtract.

sections.heading: Balances
sections.text:
In the laboratory, mass is measured with a balance. A beam balance compares the object with standard masses; an electronic (top-pan) balance shows the mass directly.
Always check the reading is {0} before you start. If it shows, say, {3} g with nothing on it, the balance has a zero error: press 'tare' or subtract {3} g from every reading.

sections.heading: Units of mass
sections.text:
• {1} tonne (t) = {1000} kg
• {1} kg = {1000} g
• {1} g = {1000} mg
A lorry of cocoa might carry {10} t; a bag of rice {50} kg; a packet of seasoning {10} g.
To add masses, first change them to the same unit: {2} kg + {500} g = {2.5} kg.

sections.heading: Mass by difference
sections.text:
A liquid has to be weighed in a container. Weigh the empty container, then the container with the liquid, and subtract:
mass of liquid = (container + liquid) − container.
If an empty beaker is {85} g and with palm oil it is {233} g, the oil has a mass of {148} g.

key_words.meaning: a reading when nothing is being measured

mistake.why: Change both to the same unit before adding.

worked_example.problem: An empty beaker has a mass of {e} g. With some palm oil in it, the mass is {f} g. Find the mass of the oil.

cards.idea: Zero the balance first, then read the mass.
example: An electronic balance with a beaker on it: press tare to read {0}.

cards.idea: Mass of a liquid = (container + liquid) − empty container.

check.prompt: An empty bottle has a mass of {e} g. Filled with water, its mass is {e + w} g. Find the mass of the water (g).

misconceptions.explain: Subtract the empty bottle, do not add it.

pick.q: Before weighing on an electronic balance, what should you do?
pick.r: Check that it reads zero (tare it)
w: Put the object on it first
e: Zero the balance before adding the object.
That would add to the reading.
pick.y: A balance that does not start at zero gives a zero error.

pick.q: Which instrument is used to measure mass in the laboratory?
A balance reads {5} g with nothing on it. What is this called?
e: The balance should read {0} with nothing on it.
Taring is how you remove the error.
Parallax is about reading a scale from the side.
pick.y: Subtract {5} g from every reading, or tare the balance.

questions.prompt: A trader at Bonaberi market has a {a} kg bag of beans and a {b} g packet. Find the total mass in kilograms.

misconceptions.explain: Grams and kilograms cannot be added directly: change {b} g to kg first.

solution: Change to the same unit: {b} g = {b / 1000} kg.

questions.prompt: An empty bottle has a mass of {e} g. Filled with water, its mass is {e + w} g. Find the mass of the water (g).

misconceptions.explain: Subtract the empty bottle, do not add it.

questions.prompt: A balance has a zero error of +{z} g (it reads {z} g with nothing on it). A bag of salt reads {r} g. What is its true mass (g)?

misconceptions.explain: The balance reads too much: subtract the zero error.

solution: The balance reads {z} g too much.
